title: Sequences and identity
summary: Generate surrogate keys with IDENTITY and SEQUENCE, and compare with PostgreSQL, MySQL, and Oracle.

items: Create and use SEQUENCE objects and IDENTITY columns.
Map identity generation across the four engines.

blocks.body: Surrogate keys need a generator. SQL Server offers column-bound IDENTITY and standalone SEQUENCE objects.

terms.definition: A table-column property that auto-increments on insert.
A schema-level object that generates numbers independent of any table.

blocks.body: `CREATE SEQUENCE dbo.OrderSeq AS BIGINT START WITH 1 INCREMENT BY 1;` then `NEXT VALUE FOR dbo.OrderSeq`. Use SEQUENCE when multiple tables share a number space or you need the value before insert. Use IDENTITY for simple per-table auto-increment.

comparison.title: Identity and sequence generation
comparison.description: Every engine auto-generates keys but the syntax and defaults differ.

migration.different: MySQL has no standalone SEQUENCE object; PostgreSQL/Oracle/SQL Server do.
migration.directMigration: Mostly yes for auto-increment; sequence-based designs need rework on MySQL.
migration.syntaxChanges: Replace NEXT VALUE FOR with nextval()/NEXTVAL; replace IDENTITY with AUTO_INCREMENT or GENERATED AS IDENTITY.
migration.limitations: MySQL emulates sequences via AUTO_INCREMENT or a helper table.
migration.whenToUse: Use SEQUENCE for cross-table keys or pre-fetching IDs; IDENTITY for simple cases.

tips: SCOPE_IDENTITY() returns the last identity in the current scope — safer than @@IDENTITY which crosses triggers.

blocks.body: SEQUENCE decouples number generation from tables; IDENTITY binds it to a column. Know the equivalents per engine.
